source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 1 (Geography as a Discipline).

sections.heading: 1. Nature of Geography
points: **Geography** studies the Earth as the **home of human beings** — the spatial distribution and interrelation of physical and human phenomena.
The word comes from Greek **'geo' (earth) + 'graphos' (description)** — 'description of the earth'; **Eratosthenes** coined the term.
It is an **integrating discipline** studying the interface between **physical and human environments** (space and time).

sections.heading: 2. Branches of Geography

sub: **Physical Geography** — geomorphology, climatology, hydrology, soil geography.
**Human Geography** — social/cultural, population, economic, political, settlement geography.

points: Systematic vs Regional approaches; the **dualisms** in geography (physical–human, regional–systematic).
Geography uses **maps, GIS, remote sensing** and fieldwork as tools.

sections.heading: 3. Approaches and Themes
points: **Determinism** — nature controls human activity; **Possibilism** — humans can modify nature (with choices); **Neo-determinism (stop-and-go)** by **Griffith Taylor** — a middle path.
Key concepts: **space, region, place, scale, human–environment interaction**.
Geography is both a **natural science and a social science**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 'Geography' term coined by Eratosthenes (geo + graphos = earth description).
Two branches: Physical and Human Geography.
Determinism (nature controls) vs Possibilism (humans choose); Neo-determinism = Griffith Taylor.
Physical geography includes geomorphology, climatology, hydrology, soils.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Determinism** = nature controls humans; **Possibilism** = humans adapt/modify nature.
Geography bridges **physical and human** (natural + social) sciences.
